messages.text: What steps did Steve take to build the LinkedIn Growth Loop?

claims.text: Steve defined the basic daily task around evaluating a targeted list from CRM context and Navigator-style targeting, drafting personalized notes, deciding whether to send or skip, and logging the outcomes.

Rather than relying on a single agent, Steve divided the workflow into two dedicated operating groups: one managing people work such as target scoring, notes, and follow-ups, and another handling public interactions like posts, cooldowns, duplicate risks, and response signals.
He set up OpenClaw as the primary worker and orchestrator to execute recurring tasks, coordinate tools, report status, and maintain lane progress.
Steve constructed a Telegram control room where harnesses reported structured updates with status, key metrics, failures, controls, and machine-readable data.
To increase autonomy, Steve routed reports, research notes, and failures back into the next agent group so the system self-improved instead of routing every suggestion through him.
He connected run outcomes and learning history with Hermes research signals and OpenClaw improvement proposals, feeding bounded changes into subsequent runs and Telegram updates.
